spec_match.rationale: farthest-corner is demonstrated as the spec defines it (hypot to the farthest corner) against farthest-side and a hard-coded radius, with the real circle(farthest-corner at x% y%) declaration used when the browser parses it.

interactive.rationale: Aspect and centre sliders reflow three live cards whose covered/gaps verdicts are recomputed from the rendered geometry on every input.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index promises the practical replace-the-arithmetic case and the page delivers exactly that, including the resize-breaks-the-magic-number story.

edge_cases.rationale: The failure mode is the demo: the once-measured pixel radius passes at the initial aspect and fails after resizing (verified covered→gaps), and the corner-sampling check is computed from the live box so it stays honest at any viewport.

conformance.rationale: Backed by the feature suite's parse assertions plus the closed-keyword-set negative; the page's coverage arithmetic matches the spec geometry the suite pins.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: initial verdicts farthest-side:gaps / hard-coded:covered / farthest-corner:covered; after driving the aspect slider to 0.60 the hard-coded card flipped to gaps while farthest-corner stayed covered — the exact lesson; console clean, no exceptions, screenshots at both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each render logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('coverage-measured', …) with ratio, centre, covering count and support flag.

design_system.rationale: Token colours only, covered/gaps states recolour border and verdict text together against light backgrounds, and there is no static-card pattern.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled sliders with visible values, per-card verdicts as text (not colour alone), and an aria-live output narrating the covering count; cards are informational rather than interactive so no focus traps exist.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; mobile screenshot shows single-column cards with unclipped text and 44px slider targets.

summary: The strongest page in this portfolio: the hard-coded-radius regression is not described but reproduced live, and on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) the unsupported corner keyword degrades to the same arithmetic with an explicit labelled banner rather than a fake pass. CDP interaction (aspect 1.50→0.60) flipped the magic-number card from covered to gaps while circle(farthest-corner) kept covering; console and same-origin network clean; no overflow on either device class. Tested at http://localhost:3000/v155/closest-corner-and-farthest-corner-radii-for-circle-and-ellipse-basic-shapes/cover-a-card/; feature /conformance/ route ran 3 pass / 5 fail, all failures honest pre-155 gaps.
